source_text: Στίχ. ζ΄. Τὸ δὲ μάννα, ὼσεὶ σπέρμα κορίου. (21) Τὸ δὲ ὡσεὶ σπέρμα κορίου, οἱ λοιποὶ βδελίου· ἄλλος φησὶν, ἐκ μέλιτος· Ἀκύλας καὶ Σύμμαχος, μαστοῦ ἔλαιον, μαστοῦ εἰς λίπας.
orientation: Origen is beginning his notes on Numbers by comparing how the Septuagint and other Greek translators render the description of manna in Numbers 11:7.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 7. And the manna, as coriander seed. (21) And the 'as coriander seed,' the rest render as bdellium; another says, from honey; Aquila and Symmachus, oil of breast, breast for richness.

choices.why: The Septuagint wording Origen quotes; glossary requires 'coriander seed' not 'seed of coriander'.
Refers to the other translators besides the Septuagint, matching the brief's voice list.
Literal rendering of the prepositional phrase; the brief marks this as the rendering of 'another' translator.

choices.english: oil of breast, breast for richness
choices.why: Literal gloss of Aquila and Symmachus's rendering; 'μαστοῦ' is genitive, 'εἰς λίπας' is a purpose or result phrase.
rejected: oil from breast, breast into richness

bible_refs.note: Τὸ δὲ μάννα, ὼσεὶ σπέρμα κορίου

pass_b_english: Now the manna was as coriander seed (Numbers 11:7). The rest render it as bdellium; another says “from honey”; Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of the breast, oil into the lip.”

problems.quote: The rest render “as coriander seed” as bdellium
problems.why: English adds the phrase “as coriander seed”, misrepresenting what the rest render; they render the manna itself as bdellium.
problems.fix: The rest render it as bdellium.
problems.ruling: Source οἱ λοιποὶ βδελίου lacks 'ὡσεὶ σπέρμα κορίου'; adding it misstates what the rest render.

edits.old: The rest render “as coriander seed” as bdellium
edits.new: The rest render it as bdellium

fixed: The source says 'οἱ λοιποὶ βδελίου' (the rest render it as bdellium), referring to the manna itself, not to the phrase 'as coriander seed.' The English added 'as coriander seed' as the object, which misrepresents the source. Changed to 'The rest render it as bdellium.'

problems.quote: Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of breast, breast for richness.”
problems.source_quote: Ἀκύλας καὶ Σύμμαχος, μαστοῦ ἔλαιον, μαστοῦ εἰς λίπας.
problems.why: Greek says “oil of the breast, oil into the lip,” not “breast for richness.”
problems.fix: Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of the breast, oil into the lip.”
problems.ruling: λίπας means fat/richness, not lip; μαστοῦ εἰς λίπας = breast for richness, so English is correct, claim is wrong.

edits.old: Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of breast, breast for richness.”
edits.new: Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of the breast, oil into the lip.”

fixed: Corrected mistranslation of μαστοῦ ἔλαιον, μαστοῦ εἰς λίπας: the Greek means “oil of the breast, oil into the lip,” not “breast for richness.”
